description: We are Vydex, a team of three from Uzbekistan interested in AI, web development, and solving real-world problems. Our experience includes hackathons and building practical prototypes. We’re looking for motivated teammates with skills in development, UI/UX design, AI, or pitching. Join us to exchange ideas, learn together, and turn an ambitious idea into a useful product.
summary:
VYDEX: Red Frontier is an interactive 3D space mission and systems engineering 
  simulator that turns the complex world of aerospace design into an intuitive, hands- 
  on journey. Instead of just piloting a pre-built rocket, you step into the dual role
  of Chief Systems Engineer and Flight Director.
  
  You begin inside the 3D workshop, assembling your probe from 16 modular, flight-rated
  assemblies—balancing power budgets, propellant margins, science payloads, and      
  launcher fairing envelopes. From there, you take your craft through an authentic 
  nine-stage mission lifecycle: staging a cinematic rocket launch, managing       
  interplanetary Hohmann transfers, and executing high-stakes powered descents where 
  environmental physics shift dramatically between worlds. Whether deploying satellites
  in Earth orbit, landing on the airless Moon, maneuvering around microgravity
  asteroids, or commanding an autonomous science rover across the Martian surface,
  every engineering choice carries real consequences.
  
  Built using React 19, Three.js, and an offline-first PWA architecture, Vydex 
  transforms passive textbook science into genuine engineering agency—inviting players
  to design deliberately, fly their own creations, and uncover what it truly takes to
  explore the Solar System.
details:
VYDEX: Red Frontier — Space Mission Simulator

VYDEX: Red Frontier is an educational 3D simulator that runs in the browser. Players plan and fly a complete space mission from start to finish. They choose a destination: any planet in the Solar System, the Moon or an asteroid. They then select a launch vehicle and assemble a spacecraft from individual components. The mission continues with a launch with realistic effects, a Hohmann transfer flight, and either a landing or work in orbit.

On solid worlds, a rover scans the soil, collects samples, inspects terrain, records video and transmits data to Earth. A surface base recharges the rover, replaces worn parts and relays communications. On the gas giants and Venus, an atmospheric probe descends by parachute, measuring pressure and temperature.

The simulation is grounded in real physics. Gravity, atmospheres, solar power, fuel consumption, signal delay and planetary curvature are all calculated from actual scientific data.

The project is built with React, Three.js and TypeScript. Its goal is to teach students space engineering and astronomy through hands-on experience.
